'''Adam Montgomery Hunt Down 90210''' is the [[Dark]] constructed list [[Adam Montgomery]] posted on DeckTech. The description (24 May 2000) says the deck "Went undefeated at San Diego Open and Alderaan Regional." Neither event is dated in the post; the wiki's [[2000 Alderaan Regionals]] (29 July 2000) and [[2000 San Diego Comic-Con Open]] were played after this post.<ref name="dt-7128">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/7128 Hunt Down 90210], DeckTech (Adam "adrock" Montgomery, 24 May 2000). Preservation copies: [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/7128/ Stephen Skilton]; [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/7128/ GitHub Pages]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261018170257/https://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/7128/ Wayback Machine].</ref>

== Original post ==

'''Hunt Down 90210'''
* '''Author:''' Adam "adrock" Montgomery
* '''Published:''' May 24, 2000
* '''Rating:''' 4.0
* '''Description:''' In immense beatdown deck that is incredibly fun to play with and not all that expensive to make.  Went undefeated at San Diego Open and Alderaan Regional.

=== Strategy ===

It won't make much sense to just read, but trust me, it works.  I generally get Vader, 2 Cadets, DJP, Trooper Assault, and Tactical Support by the third turn (usually by the second).  I put out one of my big drain sites to give me extra force and to bait them into deploying there.	As soon as they deploy *anything* to a site, I play Tactical Support to get out the three Sergeants (if I don't have them already), and commence beatdown	Let's break down the total power

Vader 6 2 Cadets 2 + 4 (TA) x 2 (DJP) = 12 Barich 2 + 2 (TA) x2 (DJP) = 8 Elsek 1 + 2 (TA) x2 (DJP) = 6 Wallen 2 + 2 (TA) x2 (DJP) = 8 Hewex 2 x 2 (DJP) + 5 (adds 1 for each Trooper) = 9

That's exactly 11 force to deploy, with a a grand total of 49 power Then, you get to use Barich's text to draw destiny and subtract from their total power attrition.  And with such a high-destiny deck, you'll probably end up subtracting at least 3.

Obvious weaknesses are against decks that don't ever plan on deploying on the ground, but I generally beat Hidden Base with this, and numbers decks are taken care of by getting Vesden out with Tactical Support.
